qs.q: A patient with rheumatoid arthritis develops progressive bilateral interstitial lung disease. Biopsy shows diffuse uniform interstitial fibrosis without temporal heterogeneity and no honeycombing. The pattern is
qs.e: NSIP is the most common pattern in collagen vascular disease lung involvement and lacks the temporal heterogeneity or honeycombing of UIP. Prognosis is generally better than IPF.

qs.q: A patient with diffuse systemic sclerosis develops active progressive skin thickening without renal failure or interstitial lung disease. Which medication is appropriate to slow the underlying disease process by targeting active inflammation?
qs.e: Methotrexate is used for active skin inflammation in systemic sclerosis provided there is no ILD or renal failure. Bosentan is specifically used for digital ulcers and pulmonary arterial hypertension rather than skin thickening.

qs.q: Which diagnostic imaging modality is considered essential for screening and diagnosing interstitial lung disease (ILD) in a patient with systemic sclerosis?
qs.e: Chest X-rays are not diagnostic for interstitial lung disease in systemic sclerosis, making high-resolution CT (HRCT) combined with pulmonary function tests necessary. HRCT clearly detects the characteristic fibrosing interstitial pneumonia at the lung bases.

qs.q: What is the standard of care treatment induction used for systemic sclerosis-related interstitial lung disease (ILD) to improve dyspnea and pulmonary function tests?
qs.e: Cyclophosphamide is the standard of care used for treatment induction in systemic sclerosis-related ILD. Calcium channel blockers and bosentan are used primarily for Raynaud's phenomenon and digital ulcers or PAH, respectively.

qs.q: A patient with systemic sclerosis undergoes pulmonary function testing. Which pattern of findings is classically expected in a patient who has developed interstitial lung disease?
o: Low FVC with a normal FEV1/FVC ratio
Elevated FVC with a low FEV1/FVC ratio
Isolated reduction in total lung capacity
Normal FVC with an elevated DLCO
qs.e: Pulmonary function testing in ILD typically shows a restrictive pattern characterized by a low FVC, low DLCO, and a normal or high FEV1/FVC ratio. Airway obstruction with a low ratio is not characteristic of primary fibrosing ILD.

qs.q: Which pulmonary function test pattern is classically found in interstitial lung disease associated with systemic sclerosis?
o: Restrictive pattern with low FVC, low residual volume, and low DLCO
Obstructive pattern with high FEV1/FVC ratio and normal DLCO value
Mixed pattern with elevated total lung capacity and normal DLCO value
Isolated reduction in residual volume with completely preserved FVC
qs.e: Interstitial lung disease in systemic sclerosis presents with a restrictive pattern characterized by low FVC, low residual volume, and low DLCO. An obstructive pattern is not characteristic of this fibrotic lung complication.

qs.q: In regards to the prognosis of children with interstitial lung diseases, which statement is true?
o: Children with protein surfactant B deficiency tend to have a very poor prognosis
Children with Heiner's syndrome due to cow milk allergy do poorly even after milk withdrawal
Immune suppressants should never be used because they always cause disease worsening
Heart-lung transplant improves 5-year survival to almost 100 percent
qs.e: Protein surfactant B deficiency carries a very poor prognosis in affected infants. In contrast, children with Heiner's syndrome secondary to cow's milk allergy generally do very well once cow's milk is withdrawn from their diet.

qs.q: Which pattern of pulmonary function test impairment is typically seen with exposures to inorganic and organic dusts causing interstitial lung disease?
o: Restrictive pattern with a decreased diffusing capacity
Purely obstructive pattern with increased total lung capacity
qs.e: Exposures to inorganic and organic dusts can cause interstitial lung disease that presents with a restrictive pattern and a decreased diffusing capacity. Obstructive patterns are more typical of occupational asthma or COPD.

es.q: A 60-year-old patient undergoes lung biopsy for progressive dyspnea. Histopathological examination reveals patchy fibrosis with temporal heterogeneity. What is the histological pattern observed, which specific chronic interstitial lung disease does it diagnose, and what is its typical prognosis?
es.m: The observed histological pattern is Usual Interstitial Pneumonia (UIP). This pattern is required for the diagnosis of Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF). The mean survival for IPF is typically 3 years or less.

ai.summary: Interstitial lung diseases are diverse disorders of lung interstitium causing inflammation or fibrosis. Diagnosis relies on imaging, lung function, and histology, while management targets the underlying cause and supports lung function.

sections.p: Severity is staged by lung function and imaging. The GAP index (Gender, Age, Physiology) predicts mortality in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
Causes are grouped by exposure, autoimmune, infection, and idiopathic. In low‑resource settings, infections and environmental exposures are common.
Patients usually have progressive dyspnea on exertion, non‑productive cough, and clubbing. Early symptoms may be subtle, leading to delayed diagnosis.
Investigations aim to confirm ILD, identify cause, and assess severity. When tests are unavailable, clinical judgment and basic spirometry guide management.
